body.estimand_functional: Along even \(n\ge N_0\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)\Rightarrow b^{\mathsf T}C_{k,a}+s\varepsilon\), with \(\widehat\tau_n\) the terminal observed-arm difference in means

sampling_model.design: Original Zhu--Liu equal-allocation PSRR: uniform balanced initialization, treated--control pair proposals, Metropolis acceptance \(\min\{1,(M/M^*)^{\gamma}\}\), and immediate first entry into \(M\le a\).
sampling_model.units: A deterministic bounded finite-population triangular array with fixed \(k\); potential outcomes and covariates are fixed, assignment is the only randomness, and the deterministic retained tail \(n\ge N_0\) has positive-definite covariate covariance, positive residual scale, and a nonempty fixed-threshold acceptable allocation set. The finitely many rows below \(N_0\) are discarded.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(n/2\) units receive treatment and \(n/2\) receive control; there is no interference and one version of each treatment.
sampling_model.overlap: Equal allocation gives design probabilities \(1/2\) by label-complement symmetry; no superpopulation propensity is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Terminal treated- and control-arm OLS projection moments estimate \(b_n\) and the conservative residual envelope \(u_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The authors state that it is challenging to derive the asymptotic distribution of commonly used test statistics and leave it to future work.
The estimator has a linear combination of a Gaussian random variable and truncated Gaussian random variables as its asymptotic distribution.
The stationary mass is proportional to a negative power of Mahalanobis imbalance, and a later accept--reject correction restores uniformity.
Under uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization, an estimated Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian law gives conservative intervals under heterogeneous effects.
The fully interacted estimator is asymptotically most efficient and permits inference identical to complete randomization under the studied p-value designs.
A sample-based Gaussian push-forward yields asymptotically conservative weak-null inference for a broad class of rerandomized designs.
A speeded component of random-walk Metropolis converges weakly to the appropriate Langevin diffusion.
Finite-population random-partition statistics satisfy vector central limit theorems under covariance and maximal-term regularity.
The fully interacted OLS estimator is asymptotically normal and its Huber--White variance is conservative under complete randomization.
A closed-form covariate-adjusted confidence interval is obtained by inverting Fisher randomization tests, with an observed-data sufficient condition for correct randomization-based coverage.

body.tldr: On the deterministic tail where covariance whitening and residual standardization are valid, finite-population Gaussian initialization also implies that the fixed positive-radius acceptable set is nonempty, so original pair-switching rerandomization and its first-entry time are well defined; the finitely many exceptional rows are discarded. The kernel derives the joint allocation-score diffusion strictly before entry, treats the terminal crossing separately, identifies the terminal covariate score as a radially clipped Gaussian independent of a stationary Gaussian outcome residual, separates tuning-dependent search time from tuning-invariant first-order terminal behavior, and turns the resulting non-Gaussian ATE law into a computable variance-envelope interval under heterogeneous finite-population effects.

project_justification.gap: Zhu and Liu's Algorithm 1 proves equal-allocation unbiasedness and Fisher validity but explicitly leaves common-statistic asymptotics open. Fiksel gives a Fisher-exact covariate-adjusted randomization-inversion interval, while uniform-rerandomization theory conditions a Gaussian inside the balance region and the 2026 follow-up changes the design by running toward stationarity and applying a correction; none gives sequencewise weak-null inference from one original-PSRR first-entry run.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is the proposal-time first-entry law of the original nonuniform PSRR allocation, including its joint outcome-residual path and observable weak-null uncertainty under heterogeneous effects.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives eventual nonemptiness of the acceptable set from Gaussian initialization, establishes pre-entry actual-filtration predictable characteristics with a separate terminal-crossing transfer, obtains a stopped diffusion and radial entrance law, proves stopped-arm moment consistency, constructs a worst-compatible-residual critical value, and gives a fully interacted Gaussian corollary without Markovian projected scores or outcome-residual independence.

body.related_work: Zhu and Liu define the exact immediate-stop PSRR algorithm and, in their Discussion, leave asymptotic distributions of common statistics open; the process and ATE theorems target that named gap. Lu, Zhang, and Zhu derive a negative-power stationary law and restore uniformity through an additional correction, which informs the transition algebra but is not the first-entry design studied here. Li, Ding, and Rubin derive the Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian law for uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization; the boundary-atom proposition certifies that the original PSRR limit is a different object. Roberts, Gelman, and Gilks supply the martingale-problem diffusion template, while Li and Ding supply finite-population Gaussian initialization and moment-consistency ingredients. Li and Ding's regression-adjustment theory, Lin's fully interacted linearization, Zhao and Ding's cancellation under p-value rerandomization, and Cohen and Fogarty's Gaussian push-forward inform the analysis layer but do not supply stopped-path validity. Fiksel derives Fisher-exact covariate-adjusted confidence intervals by randomization-test inversion under an observed-data validity condition; that sharp-null inversion is distinct from the sequencewise asymptotically conservative heterogeneous-effect variance-envelope interval based on a single original-PSRR first-entry run.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A six-row bounded array has zero covariate--residual covariance and zero projected scores at a balanced state but a nonzero antisymmetric Metropolis-kink average. Thus a generator bound uniform over all balanced states is false. The central characteristic claim is localized along the actual uniformly initialized path and only at proposal indices \(m<T_n\), where \(M_n(W_{n,m})>a>0\); the terminal crossing is a separate exact-increment argument, and no expression containing \(D/\|D\|^2\) is used at or after absorption. The early kill test is the case \(a=1\) at \(\gamma=1\) and \(\gamma=10\): an order-one residual term, or the need for empirical-distribution convergence or extra initialization, forces a pivot. Existing exact absorption and bounded-cube calculations are diagnostics, not proofs.
body.honest_scope: The pre-entry joint actual-filtration characteristic lemma and its separate terminal-crossing, martingale-problem, random-clock, compact-containment, and first-hit assembly are open. The deterministic index \(N_0\) is derived from the existing positive liminf eigenvalue and residual-variance conditions together with finite-population Gaussian initialization: because \(\Pr(\|G\|^2\le a)>0\), the acceptable allocation set is nonempty for all sufficiently large even \(n\). Every inverse, whitened score, standardized score, stopping time, and asymptotic claim is defined only for even \(n\ge N_0\), and the finitely many exceptional rows \(n<N_0\) are discarded with no asymptotic role. Predictable-characteristic expansions hold only for \(m<T_n\); the terminal crossing is handled separately, with no singular radial drift evaluated at or after absorption. The positive residual lower bound is a custom design-relevance condition for a nondegenerate stationary outcome-residual coordinate and meaningful standardization; residual-degenerate sequences are outside the declared scope. The proposal claims only fixed \(k\), fixed \(a>0\), fixed finite \(\gamma\), equal arms, bounded leverage, and sequencewise asymptotic coverage. It excludes shrinking thresholds, growing dimension, divergent tuning, unequal arms, sequential enrollment, stationary or rejection-corrected variants, convergence of expected runtime, uniform approximation rates, and finite-sample exactness. Fixed tuning changes the drift and proposal-time hitting distribution; only the terminal first-order law is invariant.
